summary: Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher who earned her Ph.D. from Yale University. She became a professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 1992 and held visiting posts at the Bellagio Center, Australian National University, and Canberra School of Music.

Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College. She held appointments at the UCL Institute of Archaeology and University of London (1948–1962), and later at St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (circa 1987–1993), and Florida State University (circa 1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald (born 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned degrees from Juniata College and the University of Michigan, where she completed her Ph.D. under Walter M. Spink, followed by a fellowship at the University of Utah (2024–2026).
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held positions at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 1998) and the University of Manitoba (attested 1999).

Katia Buffetrille (born 1948) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her Ph.D. at Paris Nanterre University studying under Alexander W. Macdonald. She has been affiliated with CRCAO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Katia Chirkova is a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Beijing Language and Culture University and Leiden University. She held postdoctoral positions at Leiden University and IIAS, and became a researcher at CRLAO in 2006.

Katja Triplett (born 1965) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning her Ph.D. from the University of Marburg. She held academic posts at Marburg, SOAS, Munich, Göttingen, Hannover, and Leipzig.

Katragadda Paddayya (born 1943) is an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University and served as a professor of geo-archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1970 to 2008.

Katrin Querl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Munich, Kagyu College, and the University of Vienna. She has held posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Hamburg.

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and served as associate professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (circa 1964–1969) and served as a professor at Hanazono University from circa 1997 to 2015.

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a Japanese linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Leipzig. He succeeded Kazutoshi Ueda in 1910 and served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo until 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896 and later held a post there from circa 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (born 1947) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and in Paris under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, later serving as a long-time professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He spent his career at Hanazono University, serving as professor (circa 1984–2008), director, and professor emeritus (circa 2008–2014).

Katsumi Tanabe (born 1941) is a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1963–1971) and held posts at Kanazawa University (circa 1993–2007) and Chuo University (circa 2007–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University and held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, Nara National Museum, Kansai University, and Ryukoku University.
